title: Detected frequencies have nonzero coefficients
statement: Let $n,k$ be nonnegative integers, let $f$ be a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, let $P$ be a set of coordinates, and fix a sign assignment $z$ on $P$. Let $\delta$ be a rational number with $0<\delta\le 1/2$, and take a sample batch of the prescribed size for the restriction of $f$ obtained by fixing the coordinates in $P$ according to $z$. Suppose that, for every coordinate set of size at most $\lfloor 3k/4\rfloor$, its batch-based Fourier estimate differs from the true Fourier coefficient of this restricted function by less than $1/(3\cdot 2^k)$. Then every nonempty coordinate set of size at most $\lfloor 3k/4\rfloor$ whose estimated coefficient has absolute value at least $1/(2\cdot 2^k)$ has a nonzero true Fourier coefficient for the restricted function.
